t: You're at the Penguin Pool in London Zoo, in Regent's Park. It's a sweeping modernist enclosure, built in 1934 and designed by Berthold Lubetkin and the Tecton Group. Historic England calls it a key symbol of British Modern Movement architecture, and it's Grade I listed. Penguins lived here for seventy years, until the pool closed in 2004 and Penguin Beach replaced it. Lubetkin's daughter once called for the structure to be blown to smithereens. Instead it became a water feature. Lubetkin was a Russian-born architect who pioneered modernist design in Britain in the 1930s.
